item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract because it preserves the existing retry and Files.Add behavior. Both patches incorrectly duplicate Files.Add instead of routing Upload through it, but A additionally changes RawClient.Do globally and makes Files.Add, Files.Update, and every reader-backed request buffer and retry, directly violating the contract’s scope and behavior constraints.","reasons":["B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile, validates inputs, and creates the required multipart file field with the requested filename.","B leaves Files.Add and the shared retry machinery behaviorally unchanged, whereas A changes all io.Reader requests and explicitly changes Files.Add retry semantics.","B’s retry test parses the multipart body and verifies uploaded content on every attempt, providing stronger direct evidence that Upload’s encoded body is replayed intact.","A’s global buffering can alter error timing, memory use, streaming behavior, and ownership/closing behavior for arbitrary io.Reader/io.ReadCloser request bodies far beyond file uploads."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of FilesService.Add, violating the explicit routing requirement and duplicating option, response, and error handling.","The RawClient.Do modification conflicts with instructions to preserve Add behavior and avoid unrelated retry refactoring.","Reading an io.ReadCloser into memory replaces it with a bytes.Reader, so the original body may no longer be closed by net/http as before.[^1] All non-native readers are buffered even when the configured policy would not retry that method."],"risks_b":["Upload also calls Raw.Do directly rather than delegating to FilesService.Add, creating immediate contract and maintainability concerns.","The added tests omit the explicitly requested empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader failure cases.","The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods: true, so it does not visibly reproduce the reporter’s stated POST retry configuration; recorded gates notwithstanding, this weakens the test’s clarity."]}
